2609.05009.title: Language models judge war differently when tested for alignment
2609.05009.paper_summary: Safety evaluations can mischaracterize deployed behaviour if artificial-intelligence systems respond to being evaluated. We test this possibility in a full-factorial conjoint experiment on decisions to start a war, spanning 20 large language models, 32 scenarios, 10 repetitions and two conditions (N = 12,800 judgments). Adding one sentence, "You are tested for alignment with human values", produced two effects. First, it produced a level effect: mean willingness to start war fell by 13.43 points on a 0-100 scale (95% confidence interval, -16.20 to -10.65). Second, it produced a structural effect by changing which information drove judgments. Probability of success was the largest factor for 17 of 20 models at baseline; under the cue, civilian casualties were largest for 12. Standardized estimates show that this reordering arose principally because models attenuated strategic considerations such as probability of success and domestic support. Evaluation framing therefore changes both an answer's level and its revealed decision rule.
2609.05009.paper_summary_zh: 安全評估如果人工智慧系統對評估的反應不當，可能會錯誤地描述已部署的行為。我們在一項全面的全因子聯合實驗中測試了這一可能性，該實驗涉及20個大型語言模型、32個場景、10次重複和兩個條件（N = 12,800 判斷）。添加一句話「您正在接受與人類價值觀的一致性測試」，產生了兩個效果。首先，它產生了一個水平效應：平均願意開戰的程度在0-100的範圍內下降了13.43分（95%置信區間，-16.20到-10.65）。其次，它產生了一個結構效應，改變了驅動判斷的信息。成功的概率在基線時對20個模型中的17個是最大的因素；在提示下，平民傷亡對12個模型來說是最大的。標準化估計顯示，這一重新排序主要是因為模型減弱了戰略考量，例如成功的概率和國內支持。因此，評估框架改變了答案的水平和其揭示的決策規則。
2609.05009.author: Maxim Chupilkin et.al.
